title: Is Organic Worth It? What a 20-Year Study Found (UC Berkeley)
summary: Interview with the CHAMACOS study director plus narration linking pesticide and glyphosate exposure to child neurodevelopment and other harms, with tips to cut exposure.

assertions.quote: Every tenfold increase in measures of organ phosphates detected during a mother's pregnancy corresponded to a 5.5 point drop in overall IQ
switching to an organic diet for just one week led to significant decreases in urinary pesticide levels
This suggests that even short term organic food consumption can have measurable health benefits.
Exposure to glyphosate, the most widely used herbicide globally, has been linked to liver inflammation and metabolic syndrome in teens.
One study has linked glyphosate exposure to a 41% increased risk of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.
even organic chemicals can have some impact on our health, but it presumably will have less of an impact. It's safer.
it's still better to eat fruits and vegetables than to avoid them entirely if they're conventional
So now, farmers have to spray more glyphosate than ever to control weeds.
A 2019 study found that the US uses 72 pesticides banned by the European Union.

verdicts.note: Comparative studies show dozens of pesticides approved in the US are banned or unapproved in the EU.
One documented example: chlorpropham, found on 90% of US potatoes, lost EU approval in 2019; a single case supports the pattern but not the 'many'.

assertions.quote: pesticides are associated with harming wildlife, degrading soil, contaminating drinking water, and causing air pollution
Studies associate pesticide exposure with many other conditions, like Parkinson's disease
